question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Having an unpleasant smell or taste from being stale, especially of fats or oils.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Rancid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Rancid" means having an unpleasant smell or taste from being stale, especially of fats or oils that have gone bad, from the Latin “rancidus” (stinking, rank). (सड़ा-गला)
◦ Example: The butter had turned rancid after being left out of the fridge for days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Pungent (तीखा): Having a sharply strong smell or taste; often spicy or acrid rather than necessarily unpleasant.

 

• Option 2: Putrid (सड़ा हुआ): Decaying or rotting and emitting a foul smell, typically used of flesh or organic matter.

 

• Option 4: Fetid (दुर्गंधयुक्त): Having an extremely unpleasant smell, especially of stagnant or decaying matter.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Rancid" frequently asked in SSC: Putrid (rotten and foul-smelling), Fetid (having an offensive smell), Malodorous (having an unpleasant smell), Noisome (having an extremely offensive smell), and Foul (offensive to the senses).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Amicable (मैत्रीपूर्ण): Characterized by friendliness and absence of discord

2. Belligerent (युद्धरत / आक्रामक): Hostile and aggressive; engaged in fighting

3. Candid (स्पष्टवादी): Truthful and straightforward; frank

4. Docile (आज्ञाकारी): Ready to accept control or instruction; submissive

5. Ephemeral (अल्पकालिक): Lasting for a very short time

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Occurring, awarded, or published after the death of the person concerned.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Posthumous.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Posthumous" means occurring, awarded, or published after the death of the person concerned, from the Latin “postumus” (last-born), later reshaped under the influence of “humus” (earth) and “humare” (to bury). (मरणोपरांत)
◦ Example: The soldier was awarded the medal posthumously for his bravery in battle.

 

• The prefix "post-" always denotes after, as in posthumous (after death), postmortem (after death, examination), postnatal (after birth), and postscript (written after the main text).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Prenatal (जन्म-पूर्व): Occurring or existing before birth.

 

• Option 2: Postnatal (प्रसवोत्तर): Relating to or occurring in the period after childbirth.

 

• Option 3: Postmortem (शव-परीक्षा): Relating to or occurring after death, especially an examination of a body to determine the cause of death.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "post-/ante-/pre-" time-related words frequently asked in SSC: Antenatal (before birth), Posterity (future generations), Antemortem (before death), Premature (occurring before the usual time), and Prognosis (a forecast of the likely course of a disease).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Recidivist (बार-बार अपराध करने वाला): A person who repeatedly relapses into criminal behaviour

2. Sanguine (आशावादी): Optimistic or positive, especially in a difficult situation

3. Ubiquitous (सर्वव्यापी): Present, appearing, or found everywhere

4. Vociferous (प्रबल स्वर में बोलने वाला): Expressing opinions loudly and forcefully

5. Nonchalant (उदासीन / निश्चिंत): Feeling or appearing calmly unconcerned

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The solemn sound of a bell rung slowly, especially to announce a death or a funeral.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Knell.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Knell" means the solemn sound of a bell rung to announce a death or funeral. (मृत्यु घंटनाद)
◦ Example: The church bell tolled a knell for the departed soul.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Dirge (विलाप गीत): A mournful song or poem composed for a funeral or for the dead.

 

• Option 3: Requiem (मृतकों के लिए शोक गीत): A hymn or musical composition performed for the repose of the dead.

 

• Option 4: Elegy (शोकगीत): A poem or song expressing sorrow, especially for someone who has died.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Knell" frequently asked in SSC: Toll (the sound of a bell rung slowly), Dirge (a funeral song), Requiem (a mass or hymn for the dead), Elegy (a mournful poem), Threnody (a song of lamentation for the dead) and Obituary (a published notice of death).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sybarite (भोग-विलासी): A person who loves luxury and pleasure

2. Philanthropist (परोपकारी): A person who promotes human welfare through generosity

3. Misanthrope (मानवद्वेषी): A person who dislikes or distrusts humankind

4. Nomad (खानाबदोश): A person with no fixed home who moves from place to place

5. Ambidextrous (दोनों हाथों से काम करने वाला): Able to use both hands equally well

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who compiles, writes, or edits dictionaries.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Lexicographer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Lexicographer" means a person who writes, compiles, or edits dictionaries, from the Greek “lexikon” (word book) and “graphein” (to write). (शब्दकोश रचयिता)
◦ Example: The lexicographer spent decades compiling the new dictionary.

 

• The suffix "-grapher" always denotes a person who writes or records something, and the first part of the word tells us what is written or recorded.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Cartographer (मानचित्रकार): A person who draws or compiles maps, from the Greek “khartes” (map).

 

• Option 3: Choreographer (नृत्य रचनाकार): A person who designs and arranges dance steps and movements.

 

• Option 4: Bibliographer (ग्रंथ-सूची विशेषज्ञ): A person who compiles descriptive lists of books or writings on a subject.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-grapher" words frequently asked in SSC: Biographer (a person's life story), Autobiographer (one's own life story), Cartographer (maps), Choreographer (dance movements), Photographer (photographs), Stenographer (shorthand writing) and Bibliographer (lists of books).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Iconoclast (प्रतिमा भंजक): One who attacks cherished beliefs or traditions

2. Cosmopolitan (विश्वबंधुत्व में विश्वास रखने वाला): A person who feels at home in every part of the world

3. Bibliophile (पुस्तक प्रेमी): A person who loves and collects books

4. Xenophobe (विदेशियों से घृणा करने वाला): A person who fears or hates foreigners

5. Anarchist (अराजकतावादी): A person who believes in the abolition of government

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who has had long experience in a particular field, especially a former member of the armed forces.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Veteran.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Veteran" means a person who has had long experience in a particular field, especially a former member of the armed forces, from the Latin “vetus” (old). (अनुभवी व्यक्ति)
◦ Example: The veteran soldier trained the new recruits with patience.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Novice (नौसिखिया): A person new to a field or activity, without prior experience.

 

• Option 2: Amateur (शौकिया): A person who engages in an activity for pleasure rather than as a profession and lacks expert skill.

 

• Option 4: Prodigy (अद्भुत प्रतिभावान व्यक्ति): A person, especially a young one, with exceptional talent or ability.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Veteran" frequently asked in SSC: Novice (a beginner), Amateur (a non-professional), Prodigy (an exceptionally talented person), Neophyte (a new convert or beginner), Tyro (a beginner) and Maestro (a master of an art).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Autocrat (निरंकुश शासक): A ruler who has absolute power

2. Plagiarist (साहित्यिक चोरी करने वाला): One who copies another's work as their own

3. Vagabond (आवारा): A person who wanders without a settled home

4. Zenith (चरमोत्कर्ष): The highest point or peak of something

5. Nadir (निम्नतम बिंदु): The lowest point of something

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

No longer in use or practised; out of date.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Obsolete.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Obsolete" means no longer in use or practised; out of date, from the Latin “obsolescere” (to fall into disuse). (अब उपयोग में नहीं)
◦ Example: Typewriters have become obsolete since the advent of computers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Antique (पुरातन वस्तु): An object valued for its age, especially decorative items or furniture from an earlier period.

 

• Option 2: Archaic (अतिप्राचीन): Very old or old-fashioned, especially describing language or customs no longer in ordinary use.

 

• Option 3: Vintage (पुरानी उत्कृष्ट वस्तु): Denoting something of high quality from the past, especially wine or classic items.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Obsolete" frequently asked in SSC: Archaic (very old-fashioned), Antiquated (outdated), Defunct (no longer existing or functioning), Extinct (no longer in existence), Outmoded (no longer fashionable) and Antique (old and valuable).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ambiguous (अस्पष्ट/द्विअर्थी): Open to more than one interpretation

2. Amnesia (स्मृतिलोप): Partial or total loss of memory

3. Antidote (विषनाशक): A remedy that counteracts a poison

4. Carnivorous (मांसाहारी): Feeding on the flesh of other animals

5. Herbivorous (शाकाहारी): Feeding only on plants

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who eats and drinks excessively.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Glutton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Glutton" means a person who eats and drinks excessively, from the Latin “gluttire” (to swallow). (पेटू)
◦ Example: He ate like a glutton at the wedding feast.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Gourmet (स्वादिष्ट भोजन का पारखी): A connoisseur of good food and drink, valuing quality over quantity.

 

• Option 3: Ascetic (तपस्वी): A person who practises strict self-denial and avoids indulgence, including in food.

 

• Option 4: Herbivore (शाकाहारी प्राणी): An animal that feeds only on plants.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Glutton" frequently asked in SSC: Gourmand (one who enjoys eating, often to excess), Gourmet (a connoisseur of fine food), Epicure (a person devoted to sensual pleasure, especially food), Ascetic (one who denies bodily pleasures) and Herbivore/Carnivore/Omnivore (animals classified by their diet).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Teetotaler (पूर्ण मद्यनिषेधी): A person who never drinks alcohol

2. Vegetarian (शाकाहारी व्यक्ति): A person who does not eat meat

3. Sceptic (संशयवादी): A person who questions accepted beliefs

4. Hedonist (सुखवादी): A person who believes pleasure is life's chief goal

5. Stoic (अविचलित/धैर्यवान व्यक्ति): A person who endures hardship without complaint

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Having an extreme or irrational fear of confined or enclosed spaces.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Claustrophobic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Claustrophobic" means having an extreme or irrational fear of confined or enclosed spaces, from the Latin “claustrum” (a closed place) and the Greek “phobos” (fear). (बंद स्थानों का भय रखने वाला)
◦ Example: She felt claustrophobic inside the crowded, windowless lift.

 

• The suffix "-phobic/-phobia" always denotes an irrational fear of something, and the first part of the word tells us what is feared.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Acrophobic (ऊंचाई का भय रखने वाला): Having an extreme fear of heights.

 

• Option 3: Nyctophobic (अंधेरे का भय रखने वाला): Having an extreme fear of darkness or night.

 

• Option 4: Hydrophobic (जल का भय रखने वाला): Having an extreme fear of water.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-phobia" words frequently asked in SSC: Agoraphobia (open or public spaces), Acrophobia (heights), Nyctophobia (darkness), Hydrophobia (water), Xenophobia (foreigners), Arachnophobia (spiders) and Zoophobia (animals).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Recluse (एकांतवासी): A person who lives in self-imposed solitude

2. Hermit (सन्यासी): A person living in solitude for religious reasons

3. Egoist (अहंवादी): A person who thinks only of themselves

4. Altruist (परार्थवादी): A person unselfishly concerned for others' welfare

5. Connoisseur (पारखी): An expert judge in matters of taste

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who walks about while asleep; a sleepwalker.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Somnambulist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Somnambulist" means a person who walks about while asleep; a sleepwalker, from the Latin “somnus” (sleep) and “ambulare” (to walk). (निद्रा में चलने वाला)
◦ Example: The somnambulist wandered into the kitchen without waking up.

 

• The root "Somn-" always relates to sleep, and it appears in many words describing sleep-related states or disorders.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Insomniac (अनिद्रा रोगी): A person who habitually finds it difficult to sleep.

 

• Option 2: Narcoleptic (तंद्रा रोग से ग्रस्त व्यक्ति): A person affected by narcolepsy, a disorder causing sudden, uncontrollable episodes of sleep.

 

• Option 4: Hypnotist (सम्मोहन विशेषज्ञ): A person who practises hypnosis on others.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "Somn-" words frequently asked in SSC: Insomnia (inability to sleep), Insomniac (one who cannot sleep), Somnolent (drowsy, sleepy), Somniloquist (one who talks in sleep) and Somnifacient (something that induces sleep).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Maestro (निपुण संगीतकार): A distinguished master of an art, especially music

2. Virtuoso (कलाप्रवीण व्यक्ति): A person highly skilled in an art

3. Charlatan (ढोंगी): A person who falsely claims special knowledge or skill

4. Impostor (धोखेबाज़): A person who pretends to be someone else

5. Mercenary (भाड़े का सैनिक): A soldier hired to fight for a foreign army

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A doctor who specializes in the medical care of infants, children, and adolescents.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Pediatrician.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Pediatrician" means a doctor who specializes in the medical care of infants, children, and adolescents, from the Greek “pais/paidos” (child) and “iatros” (physician). (बाल रोग विशेषज्ञ)
◦ Example: The pediatrician examined the newborn baby carefully.

 

• The suffix "-ician/-ologist" joined to a Greek root usually denotes a specialist doctor, and the first part of the word tells us the field or patients concerned.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Geriatrician (वृद्धावस्था रोग विशेषज्ञ): A doctor who specializes in the health and care of elderly people.

 

• Option 2: Gynecologist (स्त्री रोग विशेषज्ञ): A doctor who specializes in the female reproductive system.

 

• Option 3: Cardiologist (हृदय रोग विशेषज्ञ): A doctor who specializes in disorders of the heart.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-ician/-ologist" medical-specialist words frequently asked in SSC: Geriatrician (elderly patients), Gynecologist (women's reproductive health), Cardiologist (the heart), Dermatologist (the skin), Neurologist (the nervous system) and Orthopedist (bones and joints).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Fugitive (भगोड़ा): A person fleeing from danger or authorities

2. Renegade (धर्मत्यागी): A person who deserts and betrays a cause

3. Turncoat (पाला बदलने वाला): A person who changes sides or principles

4. Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who flatters others for personal gain

5. Philanderer (स्त्री-लंपट): A man who has many casual love affairs

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly, especially a person who has recently died.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Eulogy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Eulogy" means a speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly, especially a person who has recently died, from the Greek “eu” (well) and “logos” (speech/word). (प्रशंसात्मक भाषण)
◦ Example: His old friend delivered a moving eulogy at the funeral.

 

• The prefix "Eu-" always denotes good or well, as seen in words like euphony (a pleasant sound) and euphemism (a mild expression substituted for a harsh one).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Elegy (शोकगीत): A poem or song expressing sorrow or lament, typically for the dead, not necessarily praising them.

 

• Option 3: Epitaph (समाधि-लेख): A short inscription on a tombstone in memory of the person buried there.

 

• Option 4: Obituary (मृत्युलेख): A notice of a person's death, usually published in a newspaper along with a short account of their life.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Eulogy" frequently asked in SSC: Elegy (a mournful poem), Epitaph (a tombstone inscription), Obituary (a published death notice), Panegyric (a formal speech of praise), Tribute (an act of praise or gratitude) and Encomium (a formal expression of praise).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Bigamist (द्विविवाही): One who marries while already legally married

2. Celibate (ब्रह्मचारी): A person who abstains from marriage and sex

3. Widower (विधुर): A man whose wife has died

4. Orphan (अनाथ): A child whose parents are dead

5. Chauvinist (अंधराष्ट्रवादी): One with excessive, prejudiced loyalty to their own group

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An account of a person's life written by someone else.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Biography.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Biography" means an account of a person's life written by someone else, from the Greek “bios” (life) and “graphein” (to write). (जीवन कथा)
◦ Example: She wrote a biography of the freedom fighter based on years of research.

 

• The suffix "-graphy" always denotes writing or a written record, and the first part of the word tells us what kind of writing it is.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Autobiography (आत्मकथा): The life story of a person written by that person themselves.

 

• Option 3: Memoir (संस्मरण): A historical account or personal narrative written from the author's own knowledge or special experience.

 

• Option 4: Chronicle (इतिहास वृत्तांत): A factual, chronological record of historical events.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-graphy" words frequently asked in SSC: Autobiography (one's own life story), Bibliography (a list of books/sources), Geography (study of the earth), Choreography (dance composition), Calligraphy (decorative handwriting) and Photography (capturing images with light).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Diplomat (राजनयिक): A person who conducts negotiations between nations

2. Ambassador (राजदूत): A diplomat who represents their country abroad

3. Anachronism (कालविपर्यय): Something placed in the wrong time period

4. Idiom (मुहावरा): An expression whose meaning differs from its literal words

5. Nostalgia (विगत स्मृति): A sentimental longing for the past

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Excessive bureaucratic rules and formalities that delay official action or decision-making.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Red tape.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Red tape" means excessive bureaucratic rules and formalities that delay official action or decision-making. (सरकारी औपचारिकता)
◦ Example: The businessman lost months to red tape before his licence was approved.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Bureaucracy (नौकरशाही): A system of government or administration run by officials rather than elected representatives.

 

• Option 2: Nepotism (भाई-भतीजावाद): The practice of favouring relatives or friends, especially in giving them jobs.

 

• Option 4: Protocol (औपचारिक प्रक्रिया): An official or formal system of rules governing procedure or behaviour.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Red tape" frequently asked in SSC: Bureaucracy (rule-bound officialdom), Formality (a rule followed as a matter of custom), Protocol (official procedure), Nepotism (favouring relatives) and Rigmarole (a lengthy, complicated procedure).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Genocide (जनसंहार): The deliberate killing of a large group, especially a race

2. Regicide (राजहत्या): The killing of a king

3. Matricide (मातृहत्या): The killing of one's own mother

4. Polyglot (बहुभाषाविद्): A person who knows and speaks many languages

5. Linguist (भाषाविद्): A person skilled in foreign languages or their study

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The belief that God is identical with the universe, or that the universe is a manifestation of God.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Pantheism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Pantheism" means the belief that God and the universe are identical, and that God is present in everything, from the Greek “pan” (all) and “theos” (god). (सर्वेश्वरवाद)
◦ Example: Pantheism holds that divinity pervades every part of nature.

 

• The suffix "-theism" combined with a Greek prefix always denotes a belief about God/gods, and the prefix tells us the nature of that belief.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Atheism (नास्तिकता): Disbelief or lack of belief in the existence of God or gods.

 

• Option 2: Polytheism (बहुदेववाद): The belief in or worship of more than one god.

 

• Option 3: Monotheism (एकेश्वरवाद): The belief that there is only one God.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-theism" words frequently asked in SSC: Monotheism (belief in one God), Polytheism (belief in many gods), Atheism (disbelief in God), Agnosticism (uncertainty about God's existence) and Deism (belief in a creator God who does not intervene in the universe).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Numismatist (मुद्राशास्त्री): A person who collects or studies coins

2. Philatelist (डाक टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects postage stamps

3. Entomologist (कीट विज्ञानी): A person who studies insects

4. Introvert (अंतर्मुखी): A person who is reserved and inward-looking

5. Extrovert (बहिर्मुखी): A person who is outgoing and sociable

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An extreme or irrational fear of open or public spaces, or of situations from which escape might be difficult.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Agoraphobia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Agoraphobia" means an extreme or irrational fear of open or public spaces, or of situations from which escape might be difficult, from the Greek “agora” (marketplace/open space) and “phobos” (fear). (खुले स्थानों का भय)
◦ Example: Her agoraphobia made it hard for her to step out into crowded markets.

 

• The suffix "-phobia" always denotes an irrational fear of something, and the first part of the word tells us what is feared.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Claustrophobia (बंद स्थानों का भय): An extreme or irrational fear of confined or enclosed spaces.

 

• Option 3: Acrophobia (ऊंचाई का भय): An extreme or irrational fear of heights.

 

• Option 4: Xenophobia (विदेशियों से भय/घृणा): An intense or irrational dislike or fear of people from other countries.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-phobia" words frequently asked in SSC: Claustrophobia (closed spaces), Acrophobia (heights), Xenophobia (foreigners), Nyctophobia (darkness), Hydrophobia (water) and Arachnophobia (spiders).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Utopia (काल्पनिक आदर्श स्थान): An imagined place or state of perfection

2. Martinet (कठोर अनुशासक): A person who demands strict adherence to rules

3. Dilettante (सतही ज्ञान रखने वाला कलारसिक): A person with a superficial interest in an art

4. Pragmatist (व्यवहारवादी): A person who deals with things practically and realistically

5. Perfectionist (पूर्णतावादी): A person who insists on the highest standards
